title: Perfect weak equivalence classes recognize combinatorial model structures
statement:
Fix a universe as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category: for some regular cardinal $\kappa$ it is generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects whose Hom functors preserve those colimits. Let $I$ be a small set of arrows and let $\mathrm{Cof}$ be its weakly saturated closure, namely closure under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. Suppose a class $W$ of arrows contains isomorphisms, satisfies two-out-of-three, is closed under filtered colimits, and every arrow in $W$ is a filtered colimit in the arrow category of arrows in a fixed small subset of $W$. Suppose pushout of an arrow in $W$ along an arrow in $\mathrm{Cof}$ belongs to $W$, and every arrow with the right lifting property against $I$ belongs to $W$. Lifting means existence of diagonals in all commutative squares against the given class.

Then there is a left proper combinatorial model structure on $\mathcal A$ whose cofibrations are $\mathrm{Cof}$, whose weak equivalences are $W$, and whose fibrations are the arrows with the right lifting property against $\mathrm{Cof}\cap W$. More explicitly, $W$ is retract closed, both pairs $(\mathrm{Cof},\mathrm{Fib}\cap W)$ and $(\mathrm{Cof}\cap W,\mathrm{Fib})$ are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations, and both are generated by small sets. A weak factorization system has factorizations of every arrow and its two classes are mutually characterized by left and right lifting. Left proper means that pushout of a weak equivalence along a cofibration is a weak equivalence. The functorial factorizations can be performed using colimits and sets in the specified universe.

source.place: Definition A.2.6.12 and Proposition A.2.6.15, under the stronger hypothesis of pushout stability along all cofibrations; Proposition A.1.2.5 for functorial small-object factorizations. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: Write $C=\mathrm{Cof}$ and regard $W$ as a full subcategory of the arrow category. It is replete: if $g=bfa^{-1}$ for isomorphisms $a,b$ and $f\in W$, two-out-of-three gives $g\in W$. Its given fixed small generating subset and filtered-colimit closure give accessibility with $\lambda=\aleph_0$, using the explicit accessibility definition in [lem-coef-accessible-intersection-generators]. To verify retract closure independently, let $f$ be an arrow retract of $w\in W$, with arrow maps $s:f\to w$ and $r:w\to f$ satisfying $rs=1$. Put $e=sr$. The countable chain $w\xrightarrow e w\xrightarrow e\cdots$ has colimit $f$, with all cocone maps $r$: a cocone $(t_n)$ satisfies $t_{n+1}e=t_n$, whence $t_ne=t_n$ and $t_{n+1}=t_n$; its unique factor through $f$ is $t_0s$. This computation works in the arrow category, whose colimits are computed at source and target by their universal properties. All chain objects are in $W$, so filtered-colimit closure gives $f\in W$.

source.place: Definition A.2.6.2 and Definition A.2.6.12; explicit split-idempotent chain proof of retract closure.

proof.text: For any arrow $a:A\to A'$, apply [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] with the given locally presentable category and small set $I$. It gives a functorial factorization $a=pi$ with $p\in I^{\square}$ and $i$ in the weakly saturated closure $C$ of $I$. Thus $p\in W$ by hypothesis. Hom-smallness, the existence of small colimits, local presentability and the smallness of $I$ are exactly the hypotheses of the cited statement. No nonemptiness of $I$ is required, and no preservation property of its extra accessible middle-object functor is used.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.15, final paragraph of proof: factor the arbitrary cobase map by the small-object argument; cellular factorization supplied by the cited DAG node.

proof.text: We prove closure of $C\cap W$ under arbitrary pushouts, rather than merely pushouts along cofibrations. Let $j:A\to B$ belong to $C\cap W$ and let $a:A\to A'$ be arbitrary. Factor $a=pi$ as in Step 2 with $i:A\to T$ in $C$ and $p:T\to A'$ in $W$. Put $D=B\amalg_A T$ and $B'=B\amalg_A A'$. Let $j_1:T\to D$, $j':A'\to B'$ and $p':D\to B'$ be the induced maps. By the pushout universal properties, $j_1$ is the pushout of $j$ along $i$, and the square with sides $j_1,j',p,p'$ is a pushout. Hence $j_1\in C$ by weak saturation and $j_1\in W$ by the assumed stability of $W$ along $C$. Now $p'$ is the pushout of $p\in W$ along $j_1\in C$, so $p'\in W$ by the same hypothesis. The equation $j'p=p'j_1$ and two-out-of-three imply $j'\in W$. Also $j'\in C$ by weak saturation. This proves the required arbitrary pushout closure.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.15, final pushout rectangle argument; all inputs provided in Step 2 or in the item hypotheses.

proof.text: The class $C\cap W$ contains isomorphisms and is retract closed by Step 1 and the retract closure of $C$. For a small continuous ordinal chain of maps in $C\cap W$, induct on the ordinal $\beta$ to show $X_0\to X_\beta$ is in $W$. At zero it is an identity; a successor follows from two-out-of-three applied to composition; at a nonzero limit $\beta$ it is the filtered colimit of the already known arrows $X_0\to X_\alpha$, $\alpha<\beta$. The constant source diagram has colimit $X_0$, and continuity gives target colimit $X_\beta$. Therefore filtered-colimit closure proves the limit case. The composite also belongs to $C$ by its weak saturation. Together with Step 3 this proves that $C\cap W$ is weakly saturated.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.15, proof of weak saturation of C intersect W; limit and retract details written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-accessible-intersection-generators]. Its set-generation hypothesis for $C$ is the definition of $C$ as the weak saturation of $I$. Weak saturation of $C\cap W$ was proved in Steps 3--4; repleteness and accessibility of $W$ were verified in Step 1; two-out-of-three is assumed. Obtain a small set $J\subseteq C\cap W$ whose weakly saturated closure is exactly $D=C\cap W$. This use is only a theorem about generating sets; it assumes no right-lifting inclusion and supplies no model structure.

source.place: Lemma A.2.6.9, applied after the closure argument of Proposition A.2.6.15.

proof.text: Here is the lifting calculation for either generating set $K=I$ or $K=J$. Fix a right map $p\in K^{\square}$. The left maps lifting against $p$ contain isomorphisms. A square from a pushout of a lifting map restricts to a square from that map; the pushout universal property extends its filler. For a continuous transfinite chain of lifting maps, construct compatible fillers starting with the given map on its first object, extend using the lifting property at each successor, and take the compatible map from the colimit at each limit. At the last object this is the required filler. Closure under arrow retracts follows from [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], as does retract closure of $K^{\square}$. Thus every map in $L=\operatorname{wsat}(K)$ lifts against every map in $R=K^{\square}$. Conversely $L^{\square}=K^{\square}$, since $K\subseteq L$ and the preceding calculation supplies the reverse inclusion.

source.place: Elementary lifting calculation for weak saturation, compare HTT A.1.2 and A.2.6.10; successor and limit filler construction specified explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] separately to $K=I$ and $K=J$. Each gives a functorial factorization $f=pi$ with $i\in L=\operatorname{wsat}(K)$ and $p\in R=K^{\square}$. To prove ${}^{\square}R=L$, the inclusion from right to left is Step 6. If $f:X\to Y$ lifts against $R$, use the square with top $i:X\to Z$, left $f$, right $p:Z\to Y$, and bottom $1_Y$ to get $d:Y\to Z$ with $df=i$ and $pd=1_Y$. The arrow morphisms $(1_X,d):f\to i$ and $(1_X,p):i\to f$ exhibit $f$ as a retract of $i$, so $f\in L$. Together with Step 6 this gives both mutually characterized lifting classes and the factorizations: $(C,R_I)$ and $(D,F)$ are functorial weak factorization systems, where $R_I=I^{\square}$ and $F=J^{\square}=D^{\square}$. Their small generating sets are $I$ and $J$.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, both small-object factorizations and the explicit retract argument for their left classes.

proof.text: We identify $R_I=F\cap W$. Since $R_I=C^{\square}$ by Step 6, $D\subseteq C$ gives $R_I\subseteq D^{\square}=F$, and the item assumes $R_I\subseteq W$. Conversely let $q:X\to Y$ lie in $F\cap W$. Factor it by the $I$-factorization of Step 7 as $q=pi$ with $i:X\to Z$ in $C$ and $p:Z\to Y$ in $R_I\subseteq W$. Two-out-of-three gives $i\in W$, hence $i\in D$. Since $q\in F=D^{\square}$, the square with top $1_X$, left $i$, right $q$, bottom $p$ has a filler $d:Z\to X$ satisfying $di=1_X$ and $qd=p$. The maps $(i,1_Y):q\to p$ and $(d,1_Y):p\to q$ exhibit $q$ as an arrow retract of $p$. The right lifting class $R_I$ is retract closed by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], so $q\in R_I$.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, final trivial-fibration lifting argument; arrow retraction maps written out.

proof.text: Put $\mathrm{Fib}=F=(C\cap W)^{\square}$. Steps 7--8 give $(C,\mathrm{Fib}\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,\mathrm{Fib})$ as functorial weak factorization systems generated by $I$ and $J$. The category is complete and cocomplete by hypothesis; $W$ has two-out-of-three by hypothesis and is retract closed by Step 1; $C$ is retract closed by its weak saturation and $F$ is retract closed by Step 6. These are exactly the model-category axioms, so they specify the required model structure. Local presentability and the two small generating sets make it combinatorial. The original pushout hypothesis is precisely left properness. The lifting equalities and both factorization assertions have already been proved. All small sets, ordinal colimits and the functorial factorizations furnished by the cited small-object theorem are in the specified universe.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10 and Proposition A.2.6.15 conclusions, here assembled directly from the verified axioms.
